source: operator-confirmed table, superseding the handwritten note in capture_20260830_234933_photo
revision_history: v1 2026-08-30: 5.5 x 3.75 x 3.5 m estimate. Superseded — 24 cm out on ceiling, ~45 cm out on wall length, and rectangular-only.
v2 2026-08-30: per-wall, heights 325.4/325.9 varying by 0.5 cm, window height 110.5. Superseded.
v3 2026-08-31: heights corrected to a uniform 329.4 (+3.75 cm on v2), window height 110.9. Wall lengths and floor unchanged.
units_note: Source values are centimetres, recorded here in metres.
ceiling_note: All four corners now measure identically, so the ground truth asserts a flat ceiling and the full 1.5 cm gate is available to the pipeline. This replaces v2, which showed a 0.5 cm corner-to-corner spread; that spread was an artefact of the superseded numbers, not a property of the room.
shape_note: Walls A and C differ by 8.0 cm (1.6%) while B and D agree exactly. The room is genuinely not square, which is why per-wall ground truth is required.

floor_vs_wall_gap.what: Floor long dimension 457.7 cm against wall C at 497.7 cm and wall A at 505.7 cm.
floor_vs_wall_gap.status: operator reconfirmed 457.7 in v3 while correcting other values in the same table, so it is treated as deliberate rather than a slip
floor_vs_wall_gap.implication: 40 cm of that run is occupied by something the tape could not cross — a wardrobe, alcove, chimney breast or built-in. Wall length and clear floor are then two different quantities and the pipeline must be told which one each gate is scored against.
floor_vs_wall_gap.still_needed: what the obstruction is, and its width, so the scoring script compares like with like

open_questions: What occupies the 40 cm between wall length and clear floor, and is it on wall A or wall C?
Is A-B-C-D clockwise or anticlockwise, and which is the entry wall? Needed to align pipeline output to this key. Wall D carries the door, which makes it the likely entry.
Tape uncertainty: re-measure one wall and one opening three times to get a spread.
method_note: Tape. Uncertainty is not yet quantified: a single-pass tape run over a ~5 m wall carries sag, corner placement and reading error, and the opening gate is 2 cm. Cheapest way to pin it is to re-measure one wall and one opening three times and take the spread — until then we cannot honestly quote a ground-truth interval, and any pipeline error smaller than that spread is unmeasurable.
openings_note: Window on wall C (4.977 m run, opening 1.413 m). Door on wall D (3.330 m run, opening 0.855 m). Both fit their walls with room to spare, so neither placement is geometrically forced — this had to come from the operator.
